newsitem.title: NORWAY: Statoil plans more exploration off northern Norway.
newsitem.headline: Statoil plans more exploration off northern Norway.

text.p: Den norske stats oljeselskap AS said on Thursday it planned to increase exploration activity off northern Norway next year, with the number of wells north of the 63rd parallel roughly doubling from 1996 to between four and six.
The bulk of the wells will be drilled near existing infrastructure in the Norwegian Sea, Knut Christian Grindstad, Statoil's northern field development manager, told the Status Weekly newsletter.
Statoil said a growing share of exploration activity would take place off northern Norway, especially with companies showing renewed interest in the Barents Sea.
More licences should be awarded next year in these waters, where new geological models were being deployed, the state oil company said.
Some of next year's planned exploration spuds were originally due to be drilled in 1996.

Statoil said two wells were scheduled in production licence (PL) 200 covering blocks 6608/7 and 6608/8 north of the Norne field in the Norwegian Sea, plus one in PL 159, in block 6507/3, south of Norne.

The company's plans also include a well in Norne licence PL 128, covering blocks 6608/10 and 6608/11, a possible spud in Heidrun licence PL 124 in block 6507/8 and a well in block 7228/7 in the eastern Barents Sea.
